title: Safety Benchmark Performance Under Quantization
original_idea: Take three models (e.g., Mistral-7B, Llama-3-8B, Phi-3-medium), run AILuminate or HELM Safety on the full-precision and 4-bit quantized versions, and measure safety score deltas relative to capability (MMLU) score deltas.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The finding that quantization degrades safety disproportionately to capability has been established by Q-resafe (ICML 2025) and other works. Replicating this with AILuminate/HELM Safety adds limited new insight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Quantization tools are well-documented, benchmark frameworks are public. Running both versions is straightforward. Good fit for medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3 models, 2 precisions each, 1-2 benchmarks. Clear comparison with defined deliverable.

novelty.reasoning: Q-resafe (arxiv 2506.20251, ICML 2025) presents a comprehensive safety evaluation of quantized LLMs covering four mainstream quantization techniques, demonstrating that quantization degrades safety (e.g., ASR increases from ~13% to 70-80% for Llama-2-7B-Chat INT4). Red Hat (2024) ran over half a million evaluations on quantized LLMs. The NeurIPS 2024 paper on LLM quantization attacks also directly addresses this. The core research question (does quantization degrade safety disproportionately to capability?) has been answered with 'yes' in multiple publications.
